nodes.summary: Let $k$ be an index of depth $d$; its reverse also has depth $d$. Sending a strictly increasing tuple $(m_0, \dots, m_{d-1})$ of positive natural numbers to the reversed tuple $(m_{d-1}, \dots, m_0)$ is a bijection from the strictly increasing tuples of length $d$ onto the strictly decreasing tuples of length $d$, whose inverse again reverses the order of the coordinates.
nodes.title: Reversal of strictly increasing tuples

nodes.summary: Let $k = (k_0, \dots, k_{d-1})$ be an index of depth $d$ and let $m = (m_0, \dots, m_{d-1})$ be a strictly increasing tuple of positive natural numbers. Then the summand of the increasing multiple-zeta series of $k$ at $m$ equals the summand of the strict multiple-zeta series of the reversed index $(k_{d-1}, \dots, k_0)$ at the strictly decreasing tuple $(m_{d-1}, \dots, m_0)$.
nodes.title: Reversal preserves each summand

nodes.summary: Let $k = (k_0, \dots, k_{d-1})$ be an index of depth $d$. To a strictly increasing tuple $m = (m_0, \dots, m_{d-1})$ of positive natural numbers it attaches the real number
nodes.title: Summand of the increasing multiple-zeta series

nodes.summary: Let $k = (k_0, \dots, k_{d-1})$ be an index of depth $d$ that is admissible in the increasing convention, so that its reverse $(k_{d-1}, \dots, k_0)$ is admissible. Then the value of $k$ in the increasing convention equals the strict multiple zeta value of the reverse of $k$:
nodes.title: Increasing values agree with strict values of the reverse

nodes.summary: Let $k = (k_0, \dots, k_{d-1})$ be an index of depth $d$ that is admissible in the increasing convention. Its value in the increasing convention is the real number
nodes.title: Multiple zeta value in the increasing convention

nodes.summary: An index is admissible in the increasing convention (nonempty with last entry at least two) if and only if its reverse is admissible (nonempty with first entry at least two).
nodes.title: Increasing admissibility is admissibility of the reverse

nodes.summary: An index $(k_0, \dots, k_{d-1})$ is admissible in the increasing convention when its list of entries read in reverse order, $(k_{d-1}, \dots, k_0)$, is admissible: it is nonempty, its first element $k_{d-1}$ is at least two, and its other elements are positive. Since the entries of an index are positive, this says that the index is nonempty and its last entry is at least two.
nodes.title: Admissibility in the increasing convention

nodes.summary: Let $k = (k_0, \dots, k_{d-1})$ be an index of depth $d$; its reverse also has depth $d$. For every $i < d$, the $i$-th entry of the reverse of $k$ is $k_{d-1-i}$.
nodes.title: Entries of the reversed index

nodes.summary: The reverse of an index $(k_0, \dots, k_{d-1})$ is the index $(k_{d-1}, \dots, k_0)$ with the same entries in the opposite order.
nodes.title: Reversed index

nodes.summary: For a natural number $d$, a strictly increasing tuple of length $d$ is a tuple $(m_0, \dots, m_{d-1})$ of positive natural numbers with $m_0 < m_1 < \cdots < m_{d-1}$. These are the summation variables of the increasing multiple-zeta convention.
nodes.title: Strictly increasing tuples

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
